question: One LDS cap has to serve every method, so it is sized for the widest. What does each method gain from a cap sized for itself, and does the occupancy arithmetic predict it?
answer: Two of the three gain, one provably cannot, and the arithmetic did not predict any of them correctly until a third model correction. bi-grid runs 1.233x faster with a cap of 16, the two Pink methods 1.14x with a cap of 48, and grid-peps-3f gains exactly nothing because its narrowest usable cap rounds up to the same 1024-byte granule as the shared cap it already had.

latency.protocol: Four interleaved rounds after spinning the card until the shader clock stopped climbing, side 1024, 30 warmup and 60 timed iterations. Each specialised build is invoked immediately after the shared-cap build on the same geometry, so drift lands on both. The shared-cap figures reproduce the committed hip_lds_ab.json values within 1%.
latency.note: bi-grid at 2.95 ms is 1.46x faster than the paper's 4.32 ms reference. That is a local measurement of a workload not shown to match the paper's, not a reproduction of its number.

numerical_equivalence.note: Every method's checksum is identical between its specialised build and the stock 512/128 build: bi-grid -0.0062618833, grid-peps-3f 0.00317980815, grid-pink-peps-3f 0.00133563625, grid-pink-peps-4f 0.00172280008.

model_correction_second.was: workgroups per WGP = floor(131072 / footprint), introduced when the counter caught the original per-CU model.
model_correction_second.now: effective = ceil(footprint / 1024) * 1024, then workgroups per WGP = floor(131072 / effective). Waves per CU equals the workgroup count, since each workgroup is two waves and a WGP has two compute units.
model_correction_second.how_it_was_caught: The specialised builds produced three new footprints. All three measured exactly one workgroup below the per-WGP model. Fitting the granule to seven footprints gives 1024 bytes uniquely: 512 leaves 8704 alone and predicts 15 waves against a measured 13.94, and 2048 rounds it to 10240 and predicts 12.

falsification_test.why: A model fitted to the data that exposed it has not been tested. A cap of 80 was chosen because the granular model predicts 11 waves for it and both superseded models predict 12.
falsification_test.verdict: granular model confirmed on a case chosen to break it

model_correction_second.status: Recorded as the model that fits every measurement taken, not as a claim about hardware internals read from a specification. Both superseded models are still computed by hip/occupancy.py so any future footprint that separates them is visible.

occupancy.note: Every measurement sits within 0.2 percentage points of the granular model, and slightly below it, which is what a time-averaged counter should do.

why_grid_peps_3f_cannot_gain.argument: grid-peps-3f aggregates 112, so 112 is the narrowest cap it can take. footprint(112, 64) = 11776, which rounds up to 12288 -- the same granule as the shared cap of 128. Occupancy is therefore identical at 10 waves, and the measured speedup was 1.000x.
why_grid_peps_3f_cannot_gain.what_it_would_take: Reaching 11 waves needs an effective footprint at or below 11264, so a footprint at or below 11264, so a cap at or below 96. That is narrower than the method's own aggregate.
why_grid_peps_3f_cannot_gain.conclusion: Not a measurement that came out flat. A method that cannot be helped this way at all.

what_occupancy_bought.observation: The gain is not a function of occupancy alone. bi-grid went from 10 to 14 waves and gained 1.233x; Pink went from 10 to 12 and gained 1.14x; grid-peps-3f stayed at 10 and gained nothing.
what_occupancy_bought.caution: These are different methods, not one method at different occupancies, so the three points do not form a curve. bi-grid aggregates 16 channels against grid-peps-3f's 112, so it does far less arithmetic per point and is correspondingly more latency-bound. The reasonable reading is that occupancy helps in proportion to how latency-bound a method already is, which this data is consistent with but does not establish.

limitations: Latency measured on gfx1201, occupancy on gfx1151. No single part has both, because the RDNA4 host has no profiler installed and the RDNA3.5 host's checkout is stale.

The latency protocol here is four manual interleaved rounds rather than the eight-round settled harness, which could not be invoked in this session. Round-to-round agreement was not computed; the shared-cap figures reproducing the committed values within 1% is the only stability evidence.
The 1024-byte granule is fitted to seven footprints and confirmed on an eighth chosen to break it. It is not read from a specification and may not hold on other parts.
Specialised builds are one method each. They are not a shipping configuration; they measure what specialisation is worth.
No comparison to the paper is claimed. The paper column is a reference point.
